candidates.observed_friction: A real psf/requests source commit changes two modules and one test file; an agent must choose a quality-preserving focused verification instead of paying for the full suite.
candidates.assumption_to_challenge: Changed files require a new mapping or selection tool before an agent can find the focused regression test.
candidates.simpler_approach: Use git show to inspect the patch, then pytest's existing node IDs and collection/filtering.
candidates.problem_evidence: psf/requests commit 6f66281a1d6326b1b9c4ac09ca30de0fc4e6ef43 changes src/requests/_types.py, src/requests/models.py and tests/test_requests.py.
candidates.potential_value: Avoid unnecessary full-suite work while preserving direct coverage of the changed behavior.
candidates.cheapest_falsifier: Try to identify and run the new regression node using at most three shell actions and no new tool.
candidates.cost: One filtered checkout, patch inspection and one focused pytest invocation.

candidates.observed_friction: The same commit spans a protocol type, runtime model logic and a regression test, so a handoff could omit a dependency.
candidates.assumption_to_challenge: A capsule can represent this dependency more usefully than Git's commit identity and diff.
candidates.simpler_approach: Record the commit SHA and reread its complete diff.
candidates.problem_evidence: The three-file change is visible in one native git show result; no interrupted handoff was observed.
candidates.potential_value: Prevent false freshness after context loss.
candidates.cheapest_falsifier: Check whether Git alone exposes all changed paths for the replayed task.
candidates.cost: One git show; weak novelty because this family already has a reproduced blind spot.

candidates.observed_friction: A focused external test may fail because dependencies are absent rather than because the patch is wrong.
candidates.assumption_to_challenge: Agents need a new normalized error envelope to distinguish setup failure from assertion failure.
candidates.simpler_approach: Use pytest's exit code and first error block.
candidates.problem_evidence: No failure has yet occurred in this checkout; this is a risk, not an observed problem.
candidates.cheapest_falsifier: Run the selected test and inspect whether native output is actionable.
candidates.cost: No extra run beyond the selected candidate, but the evidence is speculative.

selected_plan.observed_problem: Choose a focused quality-preserving test for a real cross-file source change without first running the full suite.
selected_plan.baseline: Competent default: inspect the commit with Git, identify the changed regression test with native text/test metadata, then run that exact pytest node.
selected_plan.hypothesis: The competent default will resolve this task in at most three shell actions, leaving no evidenced need for a generic changed-line test-selection tool.
selected_plan.quality_control: The selected node must contain assertions for the changed hasattr/protocol behavior and pass at the parent commit with the target patch applied by checking out the target commit.
selected_plan.overhead: Clone/checkout, inspection, test execution, trace writing, lab documentation, verification and publication all remain visible; only task-specific selection actions are the primary metric.
selected_plan.stop_condition: Reject a new selector if the default identifies and passes the directly changed regression node in at most three task-specific actions; stop without product code.

result.selection: The first git show exposed the exact new regression node and its assertions for the changed proxy-read behavior.
result.quality: The repository-declared uv test environment ran the exact node: 1 passed in 0.81s.
result.setup: The direct python -m pytest attempt failed because pytest was absent. uv then created .venv, installed 33 packages and downloaded pygments (1.2 MiB), cryptography (4.5 MiB) and brotlicffi (1.5 MiB).
result.interpretation: The external task has real setup cost, but no observed test-selection ambiguity: Git plus the repository's native uv/pytest path completed the task at the three-action stop threshold. A generic selector has no evidenced action advantage here.

decision.reason: Do not build changed-line test-selection infrastructure from this case. Observe a different outside-repository friction where the competent default actually fails or exceeds a predeclared threshold.

failures: python3 -m pytest failed immediately with No module named pytest; this was retained in the trace and repaired through the repository-declared uv test group.
limitations: This replay used one commit whose regression test was added in the same patch, making selection easier than changes without tests.
Action count does not compare elapsed time, tokens or cognitive effort, and dependency downloads dominate cold-start overhead.
A passing focused node does not replace the external project's full CI matrix.
